subject: Payment authorization held — unexpected usage reported / paused service
messages:
From: Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@acme-robotics.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: billing@acme-robotics.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: Account paused due to payment authorization hold — usage spike?

Hi Vivek,

We just received a notice that our account was paused this morning due to a payment authorization hold. The team hasn't changed anything in production — our traffic pattern looks normal on our side. The billing dashboard shows a large spike in tokens around 03/29 23:00 UTC, but the per-call details look like many short streaming calls that should have been counted as partial responses only.

Could you explain:
- Why was the auth hold triggered instead of sending an invoice?
- Can you provide a per-request breakdown for 03/29 22:30—23:30 UTC?
- We need the service unpaused ASAP; this pause is impacting customer-facing robots.

I attached the invoice we downloaded (invoice_202603_acme.pdf) and a CSV export from our internal logs (usage_snapshot_20260330.csv).

Thanks,
Jacob Meyer
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Robotics

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Account paused due to payment authorization hold — usage spike?

Jacob —

I'm really sorry for the interruption. I'm escalating this immediately to our billing ops team. Quick answers up-front:
1) Authorization holds are triggered automatically when a charge attempt fails or requires bank verification; in this case the payment gateway flagged the charge after the batch metering run. It is separate from the hourly usage meter and is a payment-collection path.
2) We'll produce a per-request export (JSON/CSV) for the hour you called out and a reconciliation of what our meter counted vs. what your client logs show.
3) Service unpause: I can request a temporary manual override while we investigate, but I need an approval from finance for exposure > $5k. If you can confirm a billing contact to accept an emailed invoice or provide a temporary card, we can restore immediately.

Looping Marissa (billing ops) and Ben (account exec) to coordinate.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Account paused due to payment authorization hold — usage spike?

Jacob, Vivek —

Thanks for the details and the attachments. I pulled the initial metering run for Acme for 2026-03-29 22:00—23:59 UTC and attached a short CSV subset (usage_snapshot_20260330.csv). A few preliminary notes:
- There are ~9k short streaming responses in that window. These requests were unusually bursty (many concurrent streams), and our batcher aggregated partial outputs into separate tokens that counted as completion tokens when the client did not call the streaming close signal quickly enough.
- In plain terms: some client connections left the stream open, and our runtime counted those partial chunks both as prompt+completion tokens in the final aggregation. This inflated the per-token billing for that hour.

I can request a manual adjustment to the invoice and ask Finance to lift the pause pending your confirmation. For an adjustment > $2,000 we need Ben's signoff. If you agree, we'll issue a credit for the over-count and produce a corrected invoice.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Temporary service restore while we reconcile (expires in 72 hours).
- Full per-request export to be sent by EOD so your engineers can cross-check.
- Engineering follow-up: capture an example trace for one of the affected sessions and patch the streaming-close heuristic so partial chunks aren't double-counted.

Please confirm whether Acme wants the temporary restore and whether Ben should approve the credit threshold.

Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@acme-robotics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: billing@acme-robotics.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 12:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Account paused due to payment authorization hold — usage spike?

Marissa — thanks for the quick review and for the proposed fix.

We agree to:
- Temporary restore now so we can validate.
- Please proceed with the per-request export — our logs will make it easier to match traces.
- We approve a provisional credit up to $3,500 while you investigate; if the final adjustment is larger we will escalate internally at Acme.

Billing contact to accept emailed invoice: billing@acme-robotics.com.

One additional ask: could you include VAT treatment on the corrected invoice? We are EU/US mixed and need the correct VAT flag for our finance team.

Jacob

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@acme-robotics.com>, billing@acme-robotics.com
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 15:42:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Account paused due to payment authorization hold — usage spike?

All —

Finance has approved a temporary restore and a provisional credit of $3,500 against invoice INV-202603-ACME pending final reconciliation. Service restore is active as of 15:30 UTC today. Attached: corrected invoice stub (invoice_202603_acme.pdf) with VAT line clarified (VAT not charged — reverse charge noted for Acme, as per their EU entity details).

Marissa/Engineering: please send the full per-request export to Jacob and include a short note about the streaming-close heuristic change and a timeline for the patch (ETA 4 business days).

Jacob: once you confirm your cross-check, we'll finalize the credit and issue the revised invoice. If anything else is needed for your auditors (signed statement, evidence of metering fix), provide a contact and we'll escalate to Solutions Engineering.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
